A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and pseudocode. v1 ends with references; v2 additionally contains Appendix A documenting revisions. No material gaps prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents literature synthesis, taxonomies, pseudocode, and illustrative prompts. Its empirical performance statements are attributed to prior studies, rather than original experiments or data analyses.

after.justification: v2 remains a survey whose empirical findings are attributed to cited studies. Its expanded technical descriptions and change-log appendix contain no original empirical results.

M1.justification: The added stochastic-policy categories, evaluators, and expanded search pseudocode document additional existing designs within the survey. They do not establish a new or modified underlying model, training objective, or proposed search method.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation. The additional task categories and benchmark mappings in v2 Table 2, including knowledge-graph reasoning and tool-based tasks, expand literature coverage rather than datasets or scenarios actually evaluated by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against experimental baselines. Table 1 retains the same three comparison surveys; the additional frameworks elsewhere are reviewed methods, not newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: No original experimental protocol is introduced or revised. Added descriptions of cited systems do not establish changes to evaluation splits, metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures performed by the survey author.

E4.justification: Neither version reports original ablations, robustness tests, or empirical case studies. The additional prompting example and framework comparisons are illustrative or explanatory, rather than new supplementary experimental analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The expanded discussion of stochastic policies and self-consistency concerns surveyed model mechanisms, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 Section 8.3 adds literature-reported findings that ToT and RAP underperform CoT and self-consistency in several reasoning settings, and that sequential revision can suffice for simple questions. The earlier reported 10–20× slowdown remains unchanged. These are additional cited findings, not new original experiments.

T1.justification: Section 2 adds task-specific MDP definitions for embodied, combinatorial, knowledge-graph, and tool-based tasks and refines reward definitions. The general mathematical framework and existing search equations remain substantively intact; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claim of unifying task definitions, LLM roles, and search procedures remains unchanged. The introduction broadens the stated survey scope to other combinations of LLM inference and search in Section 6 and adds support for assessing research novelty as a use case.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive distinctions between Bellman-based values and LLM heuristic scores, qualifies logit-based confidence, and extends action-undoing limitations from LATS to other search frameworks. Sections 8.4–8.5 add caching considerations and research directions concerning model competence and irreversible actions, substantially expanding practical interpretation.

D1.justification: New documentation includes continuous-scoring prompts, GDP-ZERO's response-memory reuse and reward-rating details, and PRM output-head implementations in Section 7.2. These disclose details of surveyed systems; they do not demonstrate changed experiments. The survey's repository access information is retained.

R1.justification: The review substantially expands to Think-on-Graph, ToolChain, MC-DML, ReST-MCTS*, and other work. Sections 6–7 develop relationships to world-model construction, meta-search, evolutionary search, reranking, and sequential revision. Retained works are matched across renaming, including rStar's Anonymous-to-Qi citation update.

P1.justification: The policy taxonomy and search-procedure explanations are extensively reorganized. v2 separates AlphaZero-like MCTS, adds Section 6, subdivides related work, moves discussion after it, and creates separate introductory use-case and limitations sections. Appendix A adds a revision guide.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially reorganized, replacing detailed branches with table pointers while expanding framework categories. Table 2 adds benchmark mappings, Table 3 regroups policy types, and Table 7 redesigns selection and simulation columns. Table 8 expands and Table 9 is new.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the survey's comparative usefulness through clearer task-to-benchmark mappings, distinctions among policy and MCTS variants, and stronger explanations of applicability boundaries. These address gaps in v1's central comparison framework. The gains outweigh local defects, including the stale '11 frameworks' statement, a duplicated evaluator row in Table 4, and an incompletely specified TES branch in Procedure 8.
